title: Valid Palindrome II
statement:
# Valid Palindrome II

Given a string `s`, return `true` if `s` can be made a palindrome after deleting at most one character from it, or `false` otherwise.

A sequence is a palindrome when it reads identically forwards and backwards.

Constraints: `1 <= s.length <= 100`.

examples.explanation: A single character is trivially a palindrome—no deletions needed.
The first mismatch (c vs b) leaves no single-deletion path that yields a palindrome: deleting the left or right endpoint at each mismatch never converges.
Not a palindrome (y != x), but deleting either character leaves a single-character palindrome, so one deletion suffices.

constraints: Inputs are JSON-serializable values satisfying the bounds stated above.
hints: Scan from both ends; when characters mismatch, you may delete one of them.
Only two candidates matter at the first mismatch: skip the left char or skip the right char.
Check if either remaining substring is a palindrome—that determines the answer.

editorial.approach: Scan from both ends; at the first mismatch, try deleting either the left or right character and check if the remaining substring is a palindrome. The brute force tries deleting every single character and checking the result (O(n^2)).
editorial.why_optimal: Brute force is O(n^2): for each of n positions it builds a substring and checks palindromeness. The two-pointer approach checks at most two deletion candidates, running O(n). On 22 cases the optimal ran in 0.79 ms versus 1.20 ms (~1.5x faster).
editorial.pitfalls: Don't try all deletions—at the first mismatch, only the two endpoints are candidates. Deleting a character in the middle can never fix a mismatch at the endpoints.
